newsitem.title: USA: Fountain Oil sets Ukranafta venture.
newsitem.headline: Fountain Oil sets Ukranafta venture.

text.p: Fountain Oil Inc said Monday it has entered into a venture with Ukranafta, the Ukraine state oil company, to further develop the Stynawske oil field in Western Ukraine.
The company said it will have an 45 percent participation in the venture, with Ukranafta having the remaining 55 percent.
Independent reservoir engineers have estimated that the Stynawske oil field has remaining proven reserves of 14 million barrels, Fountain Oil said.

The maximum cost for the company's participation in the Stynawske project is $1 million in cash and the issuance of 580,000 Fountain common shares. Half of the cash and 30,000 shares have previously been paid.

Fountain said the remaining cash payment, along with 175,000 shares, is now due with the signing of the joint venture agreement. The issuance of the remaining 375,000 shares is subject to the project achieving production level targets. As of August 31, 1996, the Company had capitalized about $1,325,000 of expenses and acquisition costs associated with the Stynawske field project.

The Stynawske oil field is located within Europe's oldest oil producing region, and is in the vicinity of other substantial producing oil and gas reservoirs and two refineries. West Ukraine's largest petrochemical complex, at Kalush, is also nearby. The refineries, petrochemical plant and the various oil and natural gas fields are connected by an extensive pipeline grid.

The field currently produces about 280 barrels of oil per day from reservoir depths ranging from 3100 to 5100 meters. Individual wells had initially produced at rates up to 470 barrels daily. The current producing reservoir covers more than 6,000 acres, and contains two sections each with 100 meters gross thickness.

The Stynawske field is located underneath an aquifer representing a major water supply for the region. Concern about pollution of the aquifer had restricted earlier exploitation of this field. The joint venture's development plan is based on deviated drilling to protect the aquifer.
Fountain noted it and Ukranafta also have a joint venture to develop the Lelyaky field in Central Ukraine.
